finalText:
Root cause chain, all times UTC 2026-07-04:

**02:14:07** — Redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` drop: `redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED`. Cache layer fall back to direct store reads.

**02:14:08 onward** — cache miss storm hit store direct, no cache buffer. Store overload start: repeat `TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)` across api/worker-1/worker-2/scheduler, every ~2sec, nonstop for 17 min.

**Queue depth climb steady**, 52 at 02:14:12 up to 568 at 02:31:24 (limit 500 — breached ~02:29:06, queue depth 502, never recover).

**Redis reconnect attempts fail 13 times** (attempt 0 through 12), each ~2min apart, 02:15:26 through 02:31:26. Redis never come back whole incident.

**02:31:44** — worker-2 heap out of memory (request backlog pile up, unbounded).
**02:31:45** — supervisor restart worker-2 (exit code 134).
**02:31:52** — api unresponsive, supervisor kill whole process group. **Service down.** Log end there, no recovery line.

**Root cause:** Redis instance at 10.0.0.12:6379 went down at 02:14:07 and never reconnect (12 failed attempts over 17 min). App fallback-to-direct-store-reads design flaw — no circuit breaker, no queue cap enforcement (kept growing past declared max 500), no request shedding. Backlog eventually OOM'd worker-2, cascade take down whole api process group.

Next step, if want: check Redis host 10.0.0.12 for what killed it around 02:14, and add real backpressure (shed requests / circuit break) so Redis outage don't cascade to full outage again.
